meta.tagline: Dock scheduling that carriers actually use

slides.title: Meridian
slides.subtitle: Dock scheduling that carriers actually use
slides.question: What is this, in plain words?
slides.notes:
Say: Meridian is the booking screen a truck driver uses to get a dock slot. 32 logistics operators pay us for it today.
Context: do not explain the product yet.
Transition: here is why they pay.
Time: 30

slides.title: Trucks wait 94 minutes at the average mid-size dock, and nobody is paid for that time
points: Mid-size operators run 6 to 20 docks on phone calls, fax and a gatehouse clipboard
Carriers charge waiting fees from the 61st minute; operators absorb them
Incumbent scheduling modules require carrier accounts; under 20 percent of carriers ever log in
slides.question: Who hurts, how much, and what do they do about it now?
slides.notes:
Say: 94 minutes is the median in our 2025 sample of 140 sites; at one Nordfracht site it was 3 hours.
Context: the 20 percent login figure is from the founder's prior employer, labelled assumption in the ledger.
Transition: the fix has to work for the driver, not the planner.
Time: 75

slides.title: Carriers book a dock slot in 40 seconds from their phone, no account needed
points: Driver opens a link, picks a slot, done; the operator's board updates live
Operators set rules once: dock types, cut-offs, priority lanes
Waiting time at live sites fell from 94 to 31 minutes within 8 weeks
slides.question: What do you do about it, and for whom?
slides.notes:
Say: no app store, no password; that is the whole trick.
Context: 31 minutes is the 12-site median, not the best site.
Transition: this is what the driver sees.
Time: 75

slides.title: One screen replaces the phone, the fax and the gatehouse clipboard
points: Live at 32 operators and 61 sites since March 2025
48,000 slots booked by 2,900 distinct carriers
Median booking time 40 seconds, measured server-side
slides.question: Does it exist, and does it do what you say?
slides.notes:
Say: this is the real booking screen, not a mock; the three numbers are from our production database.
Context: the planner board is in the appendix.
Transition: does it work as a business?
Time: 60

slides.title: MRR grew from 4k to 41k EUR in 21 months with 2 logos lost
slides.question: Is this working, and how fast?
slides.notes:
Say: 10x in 21 months; the step in April 2026 is the multi-site plan.
Context: both lost logos were single-dock sites below our current minimum; name them if asked.
Transition: the reason carriers adopt it is the part incumbents cannot copy quickly.
Time: 120

slides.title: Carriers self-serve when booking takes under a minute and needs no account; incumbents require both
points: Incumbent modules are sold to planners and built for planners; the driver is an afterthought
Smartphone penetration among EU truck drivers passed 90 percent in 2024, so a link is enough
Every carrier that books once is a referral into the next operator
slides.question: Why does this work now, and why you?
slides.notes:
Say: the incumbents' buyer is the planner; ours is the driver, who then sells us to the next operator.
Context: the 90 percent figure is an industry survey, kind assumption, year 2024.
Transition: who pays and how much.
Time: 75

slides.title: Operators pay 1,280 EUR per site per month; 81 percent gross margin, 9-month payback
points: Priced per site per month; carriers never pay
slides.question: Who pays, how much, and does a euro in produce more than a euro out?
slides.notes:
Say: one price, one buyer, carriers free; that keeps the referral loop open.
Context: payback uses 2026 cohort CAC of 9.8k EUR; the 2025 cohort was 14k EUR.
Transition: how big that can get.
Time: 75

slides.title: 185M EUR serviceable today: 12,000 EU mid-size operators x our 15.4k EUR contract

stats.label: TAM: EU operators' yard and dock software spend, 12,000 x 150k EUR (assumption)
SAM: 12,000 operators x 15.4k EUR current contract (assumption)

points: Operator count from Eurostat NACE H52 size classes, 2024; contract value from our own 32 contracts
slides.question: How big can this get, and how do you know?
slides.notes:
Say: we size on our own price, not the incumbents'.
Context: TAM uses a 150k EUR total software spend assumption; SOM is a projection.
Transition: and how we get there, one motion.
Time: 60

slides.title: Founder-led sales closes a 15k EUR contract in 34 days; 9 of 32 customers came from carrier referrals
points: Beachhead: German and Benelux operators with 6 to 20 docks
Motion: a 20-minute demo on the operator's own carrier list, pilot on one dock, expand
Next: two account executives from Q1 2027, each targeting 2 sites per month
slides.question: How do you get customers repeatably, and what does one cost?
slides.notes:
Say: the pilot is on one dock; expansion to the site is where the contract value comes from.
Context: AE productivity of 2 sites per month is a plan, not yet observed.
Transition: who else the operator could buy from.
Time: 60

slides.title: Only Meridian lets a carrier book without an account; the two incumbents require one
slides.question: Why will you win against the obvious alternatives?
slides.notes:
Say: the incumbent wins on integrations; we win on adoption, and adoption is what the operator actually pays for.
Context: competitor figures from public pricing and 11 customer interviews, labelled assumption.
Transition: the people doing this.
Time: 60

Transition: what the next 24 months look like.
Time: 60

slides.title: Projection: 200k EUR MRR by October 2028, driven by 4 AEs closing 2 sites each per month
points: 2 AEs from Q1 2027, 4 from Q1 2028
2 new sites per AE per month at a 15.4k EUR contract
NRR held at 110 percent, below the observed 118
Logo churn 6 percent a year
slides.question: What does the next 24 months look like, and what drives it?
slides.notes:
Say: this is a projection; the levers are AE count and sites per AE.
Context: NRR assumed below the observed 118 percent on purpose.
Transition: which is what the round pays for.
Time: 60

slides.subtitle: To reach 200k EUR MRR and 150 sites in 24 months, one close, runway to month 24

slides.title: How a booking flows through the system
slides.html:
Carrier linkDriver opens the operator's link on a phone. No account, no app.
Rules engineDock types, cut-offs and priority lanes decide which slots are offered.
Operator boardUpdates live; the planner intervenes only on exceptions.
AnalyticsWaiting time per site and carrier, exported monthly.
